archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area)
archetype.definition: A quarterback in a run-first offense who is asked to move the chains underneath and through the middle, with little of the downfield accuracy or rushing volume that once lifted his ceiling.

report.headline: Last year's leap is fading: short passes work, everything downfield has collapsed.
report.take:
Daniel Jones's career has two good seasons, 2022 and 2025, around a long stretch of below-average football. Last year in Indianapolis was the best of them: 8.08 yards per attempt (7th in the league), +0.193 EPA per play and a +2.3 CPOE. Seven games into 2026, almost all of that is gone. He sits 38th of 45 in EPA per dropback at -0.139, 38th in yards per attempt at 5.83, and his CPOE has fallen 6.5 points to -4.21. That looks much more like his 2019-2024 baseline than his 2025 form, and in some ways it is worse.

The depth split explains most of it. Under 10 air yards he is fine: a 70.6% completion rate, positive EPA, all four of his touchdown passes and only two interceptions. From 10 yards out he completes 36.8% with a -11.8 CPOE, no touchdowns and five of his seven picks. On throws of 20+ yards he is 13.8% with a -23.8 CPOE, and those 29 attempts have cost 13.1 points. Pressure is not the main driver. His 20.8% pressure rate and 28.3% pressure-to-sack rate are both mid-pack. The ball itself is the problem: his bad-throw rate is up to 14.6% from 11.7%, he holds it longer than a year ago, and he is throwing into tight windows less often. He is missing throws, not getting buried.

The raw numbers hide a few things. The Colts run the ball well (4th in rush EPA) and pass less than situations call for, so his workload is shaped around short throws. His own designed runs are hugely efficient (+0.885 EPA, 90.9% success) but mostly short-yardage keepers at 2.09 yards a carry, not the open-field rushing of his Giants years. Three lost fumbles (42nd of 45) carry some bad luck. A 1.7% touchdown rate should drift up a little, though his career says low touchdown rates are normal for him. The middle of the field (+0.247 EPA) works, while the left side bleeds points.

The recent path is not encouraging. Over the last three games the Colts are 0-3, his CPOE is -7.5 and his sack rate has climbed to 9.2%. EPA per dropback is slightly better than his season mark only because the Week 4 dud at Washington dropped out of that window. Now his most efficient non-WR target, Tyler Warren, is out, and a division road game at Jacksonville takes away exactly what he does well.

strengths.title: Short game and the middle
strengths.body: Inside 10 air yards he is an efficient, accurate passer: +0.148 EPA on 0-9 yard throws, a 69% completion rate, better than a 50% success rate and all four touchdown passes. Throws to the middle of the field carry +0.247 EPA. This is the stable core of the offense and fits his career, since his best seasons were built on a low aDOT and quick completions.

strengths.title: Short-yardage legs in a strong run game
strengths.body: His 11 designed runs have produced +0.885 EPA a play with a 90.9% success rate and a touchdown. These are conversions, not chunk gains, at 2.09 yards a carry. The team's 4th-ranked rushing EPA keeps the offense on schedule around him. The efficiency rate will cool on such a small sample, but the role is real.

concerns.title: Nothing works past 10 yards
concerns.body: On 76 throws of 10+ air yards he completes 36.8% with a -11.8 CPOE and five interceptions. Deep balls are hitting at 13.8%. This is a genuine accuracy failure, not a low-percentage-by-design shot profile, because his intermediate throws are also off target and are where most of the picks come from. Some bounce-back is plausible after last year, but seven games of this is more than noise.

concerns.title: Accuracy has regressed, and lately more
concerns.body: His CPOE is down 6.5 points from 2025 and his bad-throw rate has risen to 14.6%, back toward his early-Giants levels. The last three games are worse still at a -7.5 CPOE. His 2022 and 2025 seasons look more like peaks than a new floor.

concerns.title: Giveaways and drive-killing sacks
concerns.body: Seven interceptions rank 41st and three lost fumbles rank 42nd. Over the last three games his sack rate has climbed to 9.2%. The fumbles should regress somewhat. The interceptions track his downfield misses and are likelier to persist, and the sacks reflect a line in the bottom third in hits allowed.

trend.note: Outside a sharp Week 2 at Kansas City, every game has been negative by passing EPA. Over the last three his completion rate, CPOE and sack rate have all moved the wrong way while the Colts went 0-3.

nextGame.headline: Jacksonville smothers the short game he lives on
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville's defense is built almost perfectly against him. It ranks 1st in EPA allowed on short throws, the one area where Jones produces. It also ranks 4th against the run, which takes away the Colts' best way of staying on schedule. The opening is deep, where Jacksonville ranks 29th, but that is exactly the throw Jones has not been able to complete. The Jaguars' offense is 4th in passing EPA and the Book has the Colts as 7.5-point underdogs at +310. That points to a trailing script, and his EPA when down two scores is -0.468. Jacksonville's 2nd-strongest pass funnel and the 293 yards a game it allows to quarterbacks give him volume, so empty yardage is realistic even if efficiency is not.

Tyler Warren is out with a groin injury. He has played 91% of snaps, drawn 36 targets at +0.227 EPA each, and been the reliable middle-of-the-field option that suits Jones best. Alec Pierce stays on injured reserve. More targets will flow to Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and also to Laquon Treadwell, who has produced almost nothing per target. On the other side, starting safety Antonio Johnson (ankle) and corner Montaric Brown (hamstring) are questionable, which could soften the deep coverage further if Jones can finally connect. The early forecast shows a chance of thunderstorms with wind in the low teens. That is worth watching, but it is not yet a factor.

keyMatchups.title: His short game vs. the best short defense
keyMatchups.body: Jones's under-10 throws carry positive EPA, while Jacksonville allows the least EPA in the league on short passes. If the underneath offense stalls, he has no proven second option.

keyMatchups.title: A deep invitation he can't accept
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville ranks 29th in deep EPA allowed, which is the softest spot on the defense. Jones's deep throws have been his worst play type all season. A couple of hits would change the game, but nothing in his season suggests they are likely.

keyMatchups.title: Run wall pushes him into a trailing script
keyMatchups.body: A top-4 run defense and a strong pass funnel will force the Colts into the air. As a big underdog, they could spend long stretches behind on the scoreboard, where his EPA collapses. Jacksonville's low sack rate is the one break for his protection.

nextGame.watch: Whether he completes even two or three throws beyond 10 yards with Warren out, because the short game alone will not work against this defense.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect something close to the Jones of 2019-2024: functional underneath, a below-average passer overall, and a bit better than this. The short game, the run-game support and the volume are sustainable. A 1.7% touchdown rate and three lost fumbles are the most likely to move in his favor, so roughly 195-225 passing yards and somewhere between 0.6 and 1.1 touchdowns a game is a fair band. The downfield accuracy is the hinge. Last year proves he can hit those throws, but his bad-throw rate and the last three games point the other way, and the interceptions come with that profile.

Warren's return would restore his best middle-of-the-field target and lift the floor. Until then the target tree beyond Downs and Allen is thin. With the team losing and the defense 21st in EPA, more trailing scripts mean more attempts but not more efficiency. He projects as a low-end fantasy option whose value rests on volume.
swingFactors: Tyler Warren's return from the groin injury
Any recovery of his 10+ yard accuracy
Sack rate behind a line that allows frequent hits

confidence.note: Seven starts is a real sample and fits his pre-2025 career, but key targets are missing.
